edges.cite: Go context package (context.Context carries both Done() cancellation and Deadline())
edges.note: A cancellation context typically carries a deadline too; expiry triggers the same cancel signal.

edges.cite: Trio nurseries / N. Smith 'Notes on structured concurrency' (2018)
edges.note: A task scope cancels its whole child tree via a scope-bound cancellation token.
The phase-1 termination request is exactly a cancellation flag the target polls at safe points.

edges.cite: Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns — Competing Consumers
edges.note: Consumers pull from one point-to-point channel/queue, each message going to exactly one.
It is the multi-consumer form of producer-consumer, scaling throughput with consumer count.
A thread pool's workers are competing consumers over a shared in-process task queue.
Propagated absolute deadlines are exactly what earliest-deadline-first scheduling orders on.
A propagated deadline is a request-scoped TTL: past-expiry work is abandoned at each stage.
Two overload responses to non-critical work: postpone it (deferrable) vs drop it (shed).
Deferrable audits/housekeeping are naturally run from the idle task when load subsides.
Both push non-essential processing out of the hot path to a lower-priority later context.

edges.cite: Thompson et al., 'LMAX Disruptor' technical paper (2011)
edges.note: The Disruptor pads its cursor/sequence counters to their own cache lines to avoid false sharing.
Head and tail indices are padded to separate cache lines so producer and consumer don't contend.
Both are cache-conscious layout techniques; padding trades space to control which line data lands on.
Two concurrency models: stackful user-space threads vs stackless compiler-rewritten async functions.
Runtimes (Go, Java loom) schedule green threads onto kernel threads via work-stealing deques.
A user-space runtime scheduler multiplexes many green threads onto fewer kernel threads.
It rate-limits interrupt delivery: at most one interrupt per batch/timeout window.
Coalesce many events into one interrupt, then drain the batch in a deferred bottom-half handler.
Under high event rates, moderating interrupts trades toward polling-style batched servicing (cf. NAPI).

edges.cite: Pont, Patterns for Time-Triggered Embedded Systems — Multi-State Task
edges.note: A TTC scheduler dispatches multi-state tasks, each advancing one non-blocking step per tick.
The long activity is coded as an FSM that advances one transition per scheduler invocation.
Both give a long activity a non-blocking stepwise structure under a cooperative scheduler.
Interrupt nesting is fixed-priority preemptive scheduling realized in NVIC/interrupt-controller hardware.
An ISR re-enables interrupts so a higher-priority ISR can preempt it.
Masking guards data shared with higher-priority ISRs that may nest in.

edges.cite: Mattson, Sanders & Massingill, Patterns for Parallel Programming — Pipeline
edges.note: Adjacent stages are producer/consumer pairs connected by bounded queues.
Task-parallel stage decomposition vs data-parallel iteration split — different ways to parallelize.
Single-producer/single-consumer ring buffers are the natural low-overhead stage-to-stage handoff.

edges.cite: FreeRTOS scheduling docs (time-slicing among equal-priority ready tasks)
edges.note: RTOS commonly round-robins tasks that share the highest ready priority level.
The rotating time slice is enforced by preemption on the periodic tick interrupt.
Fairness-by-rotation vs urgency-by-deadline: two different ordering policies for ready tasks.

edges.cite: Pont, Patterns for Time-Triggered Embedded Systems — Sandwich Delay
edges.note: Wrapping a task in a sandwich delay equalizes its duration, removing release jitter in a TTC schedule.
It bounds a section against a hardware-timer/tick time base so it always consumes fixed wall-clock time.
A schedule table is the OS-managed, statically-configured form of time-triggered dispatch.
Expiry points are offsets on a counter advanced by the OS tick/timer.
Expiry points activate tasks/set events that then run under the fixed-priority task scheduler.
The Active Object's Scheduler decides which queued method request its thread executes next.
The scheduler resumes a suspended thread only when its guard condition becomes true.
A scheduler blocks and wakes waiting threads via condition variables per its policy.
Child tasks spawned in a scope surface their results as futures joined at scope exit.
The nursery/scope spawn-then-await discipline generalizes fork-join's scoped subtask join.
Exiting a task scope requires all children to reach a clean terminated state first.
TLS is a concrete way to confine mutable state to a single thread, avoiding sharing.
Give each thread its own copy of a global instead of serializing access to one shared instance.
Pool workers keep per-worker scratch/context in thread-specific storage.

edges.cite: Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns — Message Expiration
edges.note: Message Expiration is TTL applied to messages: past the lifetime the message is treated as dead.
TTL-based expiry is a common eviction policy: entries are dropped once their lifetime elapses.
A lease is a TTL-bounded grant: the holder must renew before the lifetime expires or lose it.
A trampoline bounces CPS-returned thunks so tail/mutual recursion runs in constant stack.
The driver loop repeatedly invokes returned thunks/step objects until a final value.
Free-monad interpreters are commonly trampolined to avoid stack overflow on deep binds.
Gracefully stopping an active object: set a shutdown request, let its thread drain and exit cleanly.
Graceful pool shutdown signals workers, drains the queue, then lets each worker release and exit.
A work-stealing pool is a common executor backend (e.g. Java ForkJoinPool).
Fiber-based engine job systems balance the frame's job DAG across workers by stealing.
Declaring job dependencies as a DAG is fork-join parallelism at frame granularity.

edges.cite: Nystrom, Game Programming Patterns — Game Loop
edges.note: A robust game loop advances the simulation in fixed timesteps decoupled from render rate.

edges.cite: Nystrom, Game Programming Patterns — Update Method (Related Patterns: Game Loop)
edges.note: The game loop calls each live object's update() once per frame.
A queueing layer buffers between the async (event) layer and the sync (blocking-thread) layer.
A pool of threads takes turns as leader/followers, avoiding a separate dispatcher thread.
The Reactor demultiplexes connection events to Acceptor/Connector handlers.

edges.cite: POSA2 (Schmidt et al.) — Monitor Object (compared with Active Object)
edges.note: Both serialize concurrent access to an object; Active Object runs in its own thread, Monitor in the caller's.
Suspend/resume points desugar to captured continuations; CPS is a standard implementation basis.
A parallel reduction is the combine step of a parallel-for over independent iterations.
Stencil updates double-buffer between generations so reads see the previous state consistently.
With the periodic tick suppressed, a one-shot timer is programmed for the next timer deadline.
A cyclic executive is a super-loop refined with a fixed run-to-completion task schedule per cycle.
The periodic tick drives preemption checks and time accounting for the priority scheduler.
Protothreads give event-loop callbacks a sequential blocking-style structure (e.g. Contiki).
Recursive divide-and-conquer split vs a manager farming identical subtasks to interchangeable workers.
The master hands identical subtasks to interchangeable workers, i.e. competing consumers on a work queue.
The loop pulls pending events/messages from a queue and dispatches each to its handler.
Explicit id-based data partitioning vs implicit parallel-for; two ways to express data parallelism.
